history: Almofada is one of the many Portuguese words that start with al-, the Arabic article. Arabic al-miḵadda meant ‘the pillow’, and it came into Portuguese through the Arabic spoken in al-Andalus, as did alface, ‘lettuce’, and algodão, ‘cotton’. The Arabic ḵ sound, like the ch in Scottish loch, did not exist in Portuguese, and here it ended up as f. In Portugal almofada is both the pillow on your bed and the cushion on the sofa. In Brazil the bed pillow is usually a travesseiro, and almofada is the cushion. Spanish has almohada, from the same Arabic word, with its f turned into h, as Spanish often does.
